RagShortTexts: Mongol supervision, collection and relay work have different duties.
Messages require identifiable authority, hosts and receivers.

Variants.Content: Khanly messages, local collection and relay hospitality connect distinct responsibilities. Envoys specify authority, mounts and food, while hosts need destinations and receivers. Instructions and credentials work through actual recognition.
An escort identifies stages and receivers. Remount access does not authorize taking any horse; missing notice can leave the next host without supplies.
Princes monitor demands made in envoys’ names. Recording mounts and food prevents abuses that exhaust animals needed for the next urgent message.
Relay hosts lose farm work and care about returned horses’ condition. Acknowledgment and compensation sustain service beyond an envoy’s claims of urgency.
